source.supplement_used: In-document Appendices A-I were read; extraction uses Appendix D (rating instructions), Appendix G (diversity-change model), and Appendix H.1 (robustness checks), with Appendix A used to check intervention descriptions. No separate external supplement or posted data used.

studies.label: Study 1 (main study): car-feature repurposing, adapted AUT, five conditions

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 4; PDF p. 7, Section 4.3; PDF p. 12, Table 2 (arm Ns)
counts_source.quote: 𝑁= 502 participants. ... final sample of N = 486 participants. ... Q Question Mode 96; S Suggestion Mode 95; M Model-Led 101; V Vanilla 95; C Control 99

arms.name: Question-mode (Q)
arms.description: Human-led iterative question-mode: knowledge and analogies prompt participant alternatives, followed by targeted elaboration questions and participant refinement (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 4.2; PDF p. 19, Table 5).

arms.name: Suggestion-mode (S)
arms.description: Human-led suggestion-mode: GPT-4.1 supplies alternative ideas and elaboration suggestions; participants refine their own idea (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; PDF p. 19, Table 5).

arms.name: Model-led (M)
arms.description: Model-led one-shot rewrite of a participant initial idea, followed by optional participant refinement before final submission (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; PDF p. 19, Table 5).

arms.name: Vanilla (V)
arms.description: Free chat with GPT-4.1 in the same interface, without additional system prompts or intervention logic; copy and paste allowed (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2).

arms.name: Control (C)
arms.description: Generate and refine an idea without LLM support (PDF p. 7, Section 4.2).

studies.task: Generate a creative idea for repurposing existing car features for a new use beyond their original vehicle purpose, then submit a final refined idea.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4.1 via OpenAI API (snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; PDF p. 19, Table 5 note. The year is supported by the explicitly dated snapshot.

preregistration.primary_outcome: Idea quality, diversity of the idea pool, and perceived idea ownership: the paper identifies these as its primary outcomes in Section 4.4 (PDF p. 7).

estimates.outcome: Idea quality (expert-rated originality/usefulness composite)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: four automotive-domain experts rated originality and usefulness on a 7-point scale; ratings were averaged across both dimensions and all raters to give one quality score per idea (PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; PDF p. 22, Appendix D). When a participant supplied multiple ideas, raters judged only the first. The composite is coded overall_creativity; the component ratings are not reported separately.

estimates.notes: Main specification: linear model with condition as predictor, followed by planned estimated-marginal-mean contrasts; one-sided Holm-adjusted p-values (PDF pp. 7-8, Section 4.5). The model uses all study arms. No contrast-specific total count is printed, so n_total and n_units are null; arm counts are transcribed from Table 2. SDs are across final ideas, with one scored idea per participant, so the output-level SDs also represent participant variation. The analysis counts each participant once. No raw mean difference, contrast SE, or contrast CI is printed, and none is calculated here.

estimates.outcome: Idea diversity (cosine distance to leave-one-out condition centroid)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large embeddings; each final idea's cosine distance to the leave-one-out centroid of all other final ideas in the same experimental condition (PDF p. 7, Section 4.4). Arm levels summarize these per-idea distances. Higher values mean greater diversity. There is one final idea per participant.

estimates.notes: Secondary robustness specification of the same full-sample contrast, not an independent sample. Dunn's rank-based post hoc test; p_value records the Holm-adjusted one-sided p_adj column. The unadjusted p column is retained in the source row. Raw-scale arm means and SDs are descriptive values from Table 2. Adjustment covers all pairwise arm comparisons, including unreported comparisons. The paper provides no definition of the r standardizer. One final idea per participant; SD level is output and uncertainty basis is participant. No combined contrast count is printed. Use the corresponding main Table 3 specification in preference to this robustness record.

estimates.notes: Eligible randomized comparison of changes between two AI configurations; not a within-arm before-after causal effect. within_person is null because assignment was between people, not randomized condition order. Question-mode is the tested configuration and is coded as treatment, following the screening form; the paper uses it as the regression reference. Thus the printed negative coefficient/CI are CONTROL MINUS TREATMENT and must be orientation-corrected downstream; no sign or endpoint is reversed here. Table 13 supplies arm mean changes and their SEs; no initial/final arm means or change SDs are printed. The model includes participant random intercepts, so se_basis is participant, although observations are initial/refined outputs. The analysis sample size and interaction degrees of freedom are not printed; all count fields and df are null, with no counts inferred from other tests. Exploratory analysis (PDF pp. 8-9, Section 5.3). Initial ideas precede assistance and final ideas are AI-assisted, so this is across_people, not after_ai. Shared centroid dependence remains as described for the main diversity measure.

open_items: Study 2 randomization, recruitment details, and per-arm participant counts are not stated. Eligibility is unconfirmed for that study; no Study 2 estimates are extracted (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 6.1).

Study 1 arm-level counts at randomization are not printed. Section 4 describes the randomized experiment as N = 502 (PDF p. 5), and Section 4.3 reports final N = 486 after exclusions (PDF p. 7); the abstract instead labels the randomized experiment N = 486 (PDF p. 1). The study record uses the recruited/assigned count and final analyzed count separately.

Main planned contrasts have no printed contrast SEs or CIs, although Section 4.5 promises confidence intervals (PDF p. 8). Table 2 supplies raw arm means and SDs; no differences, totals, SEs, or CIs are derived here.
The paper does not state the standardizer used for Cohen's d or for the Dunn r effect sizes (PDF p. 8, Section 4.5; PDF pp. 12 and 25, Tables 3, 14-15).
For diversity H2b, Table 3 prints p = .984 (PDF p. 12) while Section 5.1.2 prints p = .983 (PDF p. 8). The table value is extracted; neither is silently corrected.
For diversity H3a, Table 3 prints d = 0.27 (PDF p. 12) while Section 5.1.2 prints d = 0.29 (PDF p. 8). The table value is extracted.

Diversity is explicitly cosine distance in Section 4.4 (PDF p. 7), but Table 2 and Appendix H use similarity terminology (PDF pp. 12 and 25). Direction is coded more_diverse based on the definition and interpretation. Shared-centroid dependence is not addressed by the printed uncertainty.
No transformed arm means or SDs are printed for the logit robustness tests in Table 15 (PDF p. 25); these are left null. Their main-specification counterparts retain raw cosine-distance levels.

The exploratory diversity-change model does not print its participant sample size or per-arm counts (PDF pp. 9 and 24). Counts are not inferred from degrees of freedom or borrowed from Table 2. No initial/final arm levels or change SDs are printed; Table 13 supplies estimated arm changes and SEs.

The diversity-change interaction coefficients and CIs use Question-mode as the reference (PDF p. 24, Table 12). With Question-mode designated treatment, they are printed control-minus-treatment estimates. Their signs must be interpreted using difference_is and the model description; all printed signs are preserved.

Within-arm change reporting is inconsistent: Question-mode t = 7.24 and upper CI = 0.085 in Table 12 versus t = 7.20 and upper CI = 0.086 in Table 13 (PDF p. 24); Suggestion-mode t = -2.67 in Section 5.3 (PDF p. 9) versus -2.78 in Table 13. Those before-after tests are excluded; the extracted randomized interaction rows retain Table 12 coefficients and Table 13 arm mean changes/SEs.

The Question-mode description says the LLM generated alternatives (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2), whereas the Table 5 prompts ask participants to generate alternatives (PDF p. 19). The study-level AI role is other because roles differ across arms.

Table 5 calls Vanilla Standard GPT-4, while the note and Section 4.2 explicitly specify GPT-4.1 for all AI conditions (PDF pp. 6 and 19). The tool record follows the explicit common-model statement and dated snapshot.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10. The entire markdown conversion was read in order, including references and Appendices A-I. Every cited PDF page was text-extracted with pymupdf. Table finding returned no tables on the principal results pages, so the ordered PDF text rows were checked directly. Only the named extraction file is written. No effect, standard error, combined participant count, or figure value was calculated. Numeric JSON values retain the printed value; source quotations retain printed decimal precision and signs. The primary main-specification outcomes are quality and diversity; robustness records describe the same samples/contrasts and must not be treated as independent replications. Prefer the main untransformed Table 3 specifications to Appendix H alternatives, and the main final-idea diversity outcome to the exploratory change-score outcome. For ai_vs_bau, Vanilla is the arm closest to free general-chatbot use. Descriptive AI-versus-control diversity comparisons retain both arm levels but have no reported contrast uncertainty. ai_role is other at study level: Vanilla is open_chat; Model-led is refinement; Suggestion-mode supplies ideas and elaboration suggestions; Question-mode uses reflective questions plus knowledge and analogies. There is no reported shared sample with another paper and no after_ai outcome. Separate originality/usefulness statistics are not reported beyond the quality composite. Excluded Study 2 and the technical pilot are listed in not_extracted, not studies.
